t: Section 2021(e)(1)(F) is amended by striking “2016” and inserting “2017”.

fable.w: This section is a purely technical amendment that changes a year in an existing provision from 2016 to 2017. There is no tempting reading here: it mentions no comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue. No party outside the federal government is involved in any federal decision.
fable.s: Section 2021(e)(1)(F) is amended by striking “2016” and inserting “2017”.

opus.w: This section only swaps one year for another in an existing statute (striking "2016" and inserting "2017"), most likely to extend an authorization date. It sets up no comment period, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue. It might seem relevant because the amended statute could include outside participation elsewhere, but this text adds none, so the answer is No.
opus.b: 1. **Thinking it through:** The only possible pull toward "Yes" is that the section amends another statute, Section 2021 (which, in title 38, covers veterans' programs), and that statute might involve outside parties. But this section only replaces one year ("2016") with another ("2017"), most likely to extend an authorization date. It creates no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue. Nothing in it brings anyone outside the federal government into a federal decision.
